key_insight: A deep-learning-driven pipeline enables large-scale discovery and de novo generation of functional internal ribosome entry sites (IRES), allowing programmable, cap-independent RNA translation validated by high-throughput assays.
problem_solved: Designing and discovering IRES elements for controlling translation has been slow, low-throughput, and empirical; this work automates prediction and generation of functional IRES sequences at scale.
method: Large-scale high-throughput functional assays measure IRES-mediated translation activity across many candidate sequences.
Deep learning models trained on sequence and structural features predict IRES activity and generate novel candidate sequences (de novo design).
Iterative design–test–learn loop: model-guided candidate generation followed by experimental validation and refinement.
impact: Demonstrates how generative and predictive ML models integrated with experimental feedback can accelerate design of regulatory RNA elements, providing a template for AI-driven sequence engineering in therapeutics and synthetic biology.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing data → model training → generative design → high-throughput validation loop
Sequence-space embedding (UMAP/t-SNE) colored by predicted vs. measured IRES activity
Bar chart or heatmap comparing translation activities of native, predicted, and de novo IRES sequences
Sequence logo or attention/attribution map highlighting motifs/structural features important for IRES function
paper_title: Programmable RNA translation through deep learning-driven IRES discovery and de novo generation
paper_authors: Yanyi Chu, Di Yin, Dan Yu, Guangxue Xu, Junze Zhang
